purpose: The product-docs unit is the normative English-language paper trail for Hookemon (HKMN) Product Phase 1: a clean-room, immutable Uniswap-v4-hook token launch on Robinhood Chain (4663). It fixes the approved scope (requirements revision 56, architecture revision 4), the ADR chain (ADR-0001..0019), every owner approval token and its exact bounded subject hashes, the 12 active Phase 1 tasks (P1-001..010,012,013; P1-011 deferred), the per-module contract cards, and the red-team/QA disposition. Its single most load-bearing fact for this audit: Phase 1 is explicitly, repeatedly, and recently (ADR-0018, 31 Aug 2026; requirements revision 55/56) scoped to ONE manually-started, operator-triggered, fully-reconciled cycle with NO dashboard, NO scheduler, NO periodic/20-minute trigger, and NO continuous/unattended operation. The owner's autonomous-20-minute-cycle-plus-dashboard target is Phase 2 territory that has not been opened (no fresh requirements revision, no owner approval) and is explicitly non-operative.
keyFacts: Fee split (immutable, revision 56, unchanged since ADR-0016): totalFee=floor(Q*300/10000), programmable=floor(Q*10/10000)=0.10%, treasury=floor(Q*40/10000)=0.40%, process=remainder=2.50%. Sums to inclusive 3.00%. 0.10%+0.40%=0.50% matches the owner's 'separated 0.5%' statement; repository split is internally consistent and owner-approved (product/PRD.md, decisions/ADR-0016).

Owner target of '0.5% separated: 0.5% treasury, 0.1% Programmable' as transcribed does not match the repo (repo: 0.4% treasury + 0.1% Programmable = 0.5%, not '0.5% treasury'); repo is authoritative per task framing, discrepancy is in the voice-transcript wording only, not in the code/docs.

REQ-dashboard-1 is REMOVED from the active requirements array in revision 55/56 and PERMANENTLY RESERVED — it can never be reused for a new requirement (product/REQUIREMENTS_REVISION_55_PROPOSAL.md, ADR-0018).

docs/modules/dashboard.md is explicitly titled 'Dashboard — Phase 2 Only' and states it 'is not an active Phase 1 module, interface, release dependency, risk default, or requirement' — historical/non-operative design context only.

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-manual-one-cycle-design.md line 144 explicitly lists 'periodic or twenty-minute triggers' in the 'Deferred to Phase 2' list — the owner's exact automation cadence concept was considered and explicitly deferred, not overlooked.

docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-phase-2-foundation-draft.md is a DRAFT/NON-OPERATIVE Phase 2 discovery doc; its 'Owner decision matrix' table has an open 'Trigger model' row ('manual, periodic, event-driven, or continuously evaluated?') with default 'No scheduler or unattended trigger' while open, and an open 'Pack strategy' row (which packs/quantities/selection are allowed) with default 'No automatic selection' — these are exactly the two owner-target features (interval control, pack selection) and both require a fresh Phase 2 spec + owner approval to activate.

ADR-0019 (accepted 1 Sep 2026, current) replaced Operations-directed process release with an immutable hook-bound PegCycleVault: the hook may debit process liability only while atomically funding the vault; Operations is trigger-only and NEVER receives/routes/returns/funds/withdraws/approves process principal or returned proceeds. Vault lifecycle: EMPTY->FUNDED->OUTBOUND->RETURNED->PAYOUT_COMMITTED, with an absorbing FAILED state.

The Collector Crypt pack cycle (buy/open/sell) is implemented ONLY as a fixture/test simulation in the runner (docs/modules/cycle-runner.md): 'fixture-provider', 'fixture-program', 'fixture-fee-payer' literals throughout; 'Production Collector API integration remains INTEGRATION_PENDING'. There is no real external pack-purchase capability yet — this is the single largest gap versus the owner's 'buy a pack every N minutes' target.

Owner's 'bei Bybit' sale-path statement: repository has NO Bybit integration anywhere in product docs. The only evidenced sale path is the Collector Crypt 'standard buyback' (docs/modules/cycle-runner.md, product/PHASE_1_THIN_V1_DESIGN.md); ADR-0013 evidence cites Collector Crypt's official Solana Gacha API docs. This strongly supports the task framing's hypothesis that 'Bybit' is a mis-transcription of 'buyback' — no independent evidence of an actual Bybit integration exists in this unit.

Robinhood Chain 4663 was found 'unsupported as a production launch target' by a live discovery spike (SPIKE-R53-PROGRAMMABLE-CHAIN-4663, evidence note on ADR-0001 and ADR-0009, dated 2026-08-30) — consistent with the owner's statement that the Programmable launchpad 'is currently being rebuilt for Robinhood Chain'.

qa/reviews/p1-012-local-verification.json records an online binding recheck (observed 2026-09-01T00:15:31Z, NOT applied to the release) showing the pinned Robinhood official-doc source hashes have DRIFTED: robinhood-deploy-contracts and robinhood-token-contracts both show 'matches: false' against the pinned revision-54 digests, while two Uniswap-side sources still match. Official Robinhood documentation has changed since the binding was pinned; a re-pin is needed before any further production work.

Owner-approval gate overrides for revision 56 (decisions/owner-approvals/phase-1-revision-56-*-local-closure-override.json) are explicit LOCAL-CLOSURE-ONLY overrides and each names still-open items: build gate — B6 open (P1-006/007/009/010 share one completion commit hash, no per-task commit integrity proof); feasibility gate — F3 still blocked by production integration facts; redteam gate — R4 escalated, bound red-team artifacts still identify requirements revision 55 (STALE vs. current rev 56), open high findings unresolved; ship gate — H1 open (no release reached operating state), H2 open (no alert test-fired into a real channel), H4 open (advisory review not recorded).

decisions/redteam/findings.json and all of qa/redteam/*.json are bound to requirementsRevision 55 / architectureRevision 4 (STALE — current spec is revision 56). 3 of 6 findings remain OPEN_FAIL_CLOSED: RT-R55-02 (compromised Operations identity could release the FULL accrued process liability; no onchain cap — status may be improved but not re-verified after ADR-0019's vault redesign), RT-R55-05 (no durable/long-horizon proof-recovery model for the two-copy manifest publication — blocks P1-009 completion per its own disposition), RT-R55-06 (buyer-output settlement proven only via a test-local router, not the real production Robinhood router/PoolManager).

qa/reviews/index.json 'reviewPolicy': every remediation after Task-04-style CHANGES_REQUESTED reviews was 'NOT_RUN_PER_OWNER_INSTRUCTION' — i.e. fixes were applied but never re-reviewed by an independent reviewer; index.json explicitly states 'this index is neither zero-severe evidence nor release approval'.

AGENTS.md line 1 states it is GENERATED from policy/policy.json — never hand-edit; RULES.md is the same GENERATED subset (R1-R6) without the Autonomy section. Both are internally consistent with each other as read.

product/PHASE_1_CONTINUOUS_WORK_AUTONOMY_GRANT.md explicitly names the working repository as 'https://github.com/legacy-org/hkmn.git' and forbids 'using or referencing any repository other than' that URL — this does not match the current origin (owner-devs/gacha per task framing), a naming/identity drift across the project's history.

docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-01-immutable-peg-cycle-custody.md line 610 notes: 'The owner has authorized read-only use of the historical Programmable API key for legacy API-shape discovery before rotation; if the key is made available, keep it out of repository files, command output, logs, receipts, and Git history. It never authorizes mutation, signing, deployment, publication, or Mainnet activity.' (Not accessed by this audit; flagged per the no-credentials rule.)

Total supply 420,690,000,000 HKMN, 18 decimals if supported, 90% to canonical market (permanently non-project-controlled custody, zero LP fee), 10% to an officially-supported lock/vesting or else undistributed. No presale, no post-init mint.

Distribution model: canonical depth-10 Merkle-sum tree, max 1,024 recipients, paid key (payoutId, index), permissionless non-expiring at-most-once payment. No recipient replacement, no batch/delay state, no admin/automation/pause role in the immutable hook.

invariants: Inclusive 3.00% fee, floor-division split 0.10%/0.40%/remainder-2.50%, exact conservation to actual collected USDG (ADR-0016, REQ-fee-accounting-1).
Canonical PoolKey static LP fee is exactly zero; the Hookemon hook fee is the ONLY trading surcharge (ADR-0017, REQ-canonical-market-5).
90% launch position: permanent, non-project-controlled, non-transferable/non-withdrawable/non-upgradeable custody; never freezes user trading (ADR-0017).

Operations is a trigger-only identity: never receives, routes, funds, or withdraws process principal or returned proceeds; two-step handover only affects future triggers (ADR-0011->ADR-0015->ADR-0019 supersession chain).

PegCycleVault lifecycle EMPTY->FUNDED->OUTBOUND->RETURNED->PAYOUT_COMMITTED is single-cycle, single-use, and FAILED is absorbing — no recovery/withdrawal path exists in Phase 1 (ADR-0019, docs/modules/peg-cycle-vault.md).

Payout is a canonical depth-10 Merkle-sum tree (1,024 max positions); root sum must equal exact vault-to-hook USDG balance delta; paid key (payoutId,index) is exactly-once, non-expiring, permissionless (ADR-0014).

No admin/automation/pause/scheduler/dashboard-setting role or selector exists anywhere in the immutable hook or vault (REQ-role-control-3, REQ-process-budget-5, architecture/capability-map.json forbiddenProductionSurfaces).

Phase 1 is limited to exactly one manually-started cycle; Phase 2 requires a fresh requirements revision + new owner approval and cannot be inherited from non-operative future notes (REQ-phase-boundary-1..3, ADR-0018).

Historical/previous-chain code and evidence are non-authoritative; only current owner decisions + official versioned provider evidence + derived requirements/ADRs + new tests/receipts can become Phase 1 authority (product/SOURCE_BOUNDARY.md).

testStatus: No executable test files exist inside this unit (product-docs) itself; the unit only documents test *expectations* and past *results*. Per docs/modules/*.md 'Operational commands' sections, the real suites live under packages/contracts/test/**/*.t.sol (Foundry) and packages/runner/test/**/*.test.mjs (node --test), covered by other audit units. From this unit's evidence: qa/reviews/p1-010-local-verification.json reports 72/72 runner cycle tests passed (fixture-only, no external actions); qa/reviews/p1-012-local-verification.json reports a 6-check/85-file local release-verifier PASS, 2x reproducible builds of 20 artifacts, 9 invariants x256 runs x128,000 calls all positive, but explicitly 'not release approval' and 'does not prove production readiness'; decisions/redteam/findings.json / qa/redteam/threat-model.json / qa/redteam/resolutions.json / qa/redteam/termination.json record 6 STRIDE findings (0 critical, 3 resolved, 3 OPEN_FAIL_CLOSED) all still bound to the now-superseded requirements revision 55, i.e. never re-run against revision 56's PegCycleVault redesign. qa/reviews/index.json shows every CHANGES_REQUESTED review's remediation was never independently re-reviewed ('NOT_RUN_PER_OWNER_INSTRUCTION'). No dashboard/browser test exists or is planned for Phase 1 (REQ-dashboard-1 removed).
autonomyGaps: No scheduler, timer, or interval mechanism exists anywhere in scope or code (hook, vault, or runner) — explicitly forbidden as a 'forbiddenProductionSurface' and explicitly deferred by name ('periodic or twenty-minute triggers') in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-manual-one-cycle-design.md. Achieving the owner's 'every N minutes, default 20, adjustable' cadence requires a brand-new Phase 2 spec, architecture, and owner approval — none of which exist yet.

No dashboard/UI of any kind is authorized for Phase 1; REQ-dashboard-1 is permanently reserved and cannot be reactivated even by re-implementing the old (already-built-then-deferred) P1-011 work. Pack selection, interval control, restart/kick-stuck-cycle controls, and community status all require net-new Phase 2 UI scope with its own threat model (per docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-phase-2-foundation-draft.md's still-open decision matrix rows: Audience, UI authority, Trigger model, Pack strategy, Concurrency).

The real Collector Crypt pack purchase/open/buyback loop is fixture-only in the runner today; production API integration, credential handling, and Solana broadcast are all INTEGRATION_PENDING. 'Buy a pack automatically' cannot happen until this is built and bound to real evidence, then separately owner-authorized per action (cycle-runner.md; PHASE_1_THIN_V1_DESIGN.md 'Release proof').

'Restart/kick stuck cycles' implies an operator-recovery capability; today a stranded PegCycleVault cycle after external-execution failure has NO recovery/withdrawal path by design ('FAILED is absorbing... no recovery withdrawal', ADR-0019/peg-cycle-vault design doc) — any future kick/restart mechanism is a new authority surface that must be spec'd, not an operational toggle.

'Choose which packs to buy' (multi-pack / pack-selection policy) is explicitly out of scope for the immutable hook and reversible runner alike; V1 freezes exactly one operator-selected pack per cycle into the cycle authorization before execution — no catalog, no selection algorithm exists.

Continuous/unattended operation with no operator in the loop directly contradicts the owner-approved AGENTS.md Autonomy 'Ask first' list item 'Any spend, credential use, or secret access' and the repository's universal per-action owner-authorization requirement (TB-01, TB-11, TB-19) — every external mutation (conversion, pack purchase, buyback, broadcast) is designed to pause for a fresh, single-use, action-specific owner authorization. A fully unattended 20-minute loop is architecturally incompatible with the current design's per-action authorization model unless the owner explicitly grants a new standing authority in a Phase 2 spec.

No alerting/monitoring channel has ever been test-fired (qa/drills/induced-failure.json: alertChannelTested:false; ship-gate override H2 open) — 'community-facing status' has no even-draft implementation or design yet beyond the deferred read-only dashboard sketch.

suspicions.note: Card's Purpose line says 'This module validates the revision-54, architecture-revision-3 build contract' while every other current artifact (docs/modules/index.json, architecture/interfaces.json, specs/requirements.json) is on requirements revision 56 / architecture revision 4. Stale revision reference left in prose after later revisions shipped.

Domain separator string is hardcoded as keccak256("HOOKEMON_CANONICAL_SWAP_R54_A3_V1") — bakes revision 54/architecture 3 into an onchain constant name even though the module is otherwise described as revision-56 code; functionally harmless (it's just a label) but confirms code lags spec-revision bumps.

Operational command hardcodes a machine-specific path: 'HOOKEMON_SOLC_BINARY=/private/tmp/p1-004-solc-0.8.26' — same absolute-tmp-path pattern recurs across docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-01-immutable-peg-cycle-custody.md (e.g. lines 165, 251, 319-321, 388, 443, 534, 540-542) and qa/drills/induced-failure.json line 12 ('/private/tmp/node-v24.19.0-darwin-arm64/bin/node'). These are non-portable, author-machine-specific paths embedded as if they were reproducible commands; a fresh environment (like this worktree) cannot run them as written.

'CURRENT TODOS' list contains only 'P1-013' itself, unlike every other task card (P1-001..012) which lists the full 11/12-item Phase 1 backlog. Looks like P1-013 (added later per git log 'feat(hook): integrate canonical v4 accounting') was never resynced with the other cards' shared TODO block — a doc-generation/sync gap, not a functional defect.

Hard-stop list names 'using or referencing any repository other than https://github.com/legacy-org/hkmn.git' — that URL does not match the current origin (owner-devs/gacha, per task framing). Either the project migrated identity/org at some point without updating this grant doc, or this grant is itself stale/superseded evidence; worth confirming with the owner which repo is now authoritative.

requirementsRevision:55 — the entire red-team findings/threat-model/resolutions/termination/doubt-loop artifact set (qa/redteam/*.json + decisions/redteam/findings.json) was never regenerated against requirements revision 56's PegCycleVault redesign (ADR-0019). RT-R55-02's 'compromised Operations releases full liability' finding may be partially mitigated by the vault redesign (Operations can no longer receive the funds, only trigger their move into an equally-liable-but-still-immutable vault) but this has not been independently re-assessed — the finding is carried forward unverified rather than re-scoped.

'secondReviewAfterFixes: NOT_RUN_PER_OWNER_INSTRUCTION' applied to every CHANGES_REQUESTED review in the file (5 of 6 entries) — every remediation for every flagged finding across P1-GATE-FAIL-CLOSED, P1-REPRODUCIBILITY, P1-RELEASE-VERIFIER, and P1-012-RELEASE-HARNESS was self-verified by re-running the same focused tests but never independently re-reviewed by a fresh reviewer, despite AGENTS.md's own R3/R4-risk-class doubt-loop control requiring 'fresh-context-independent-reviewer' for R3/R4 work. This is an owner-instructed process shortcut, not a hidden defect, but it means every 'REMEDIATED_LOCALLY_NOT_RE_REVIEWED' disposition carries less assurance than the original review pass.

Override rationale explicitly states the bound red-team artifacts 'still identify requirements revision 55' at override time — the owner knowingly overrode a stale-evidence gate rather than waiting for regeneration; this is documented and intentional, but any future automated status check should treat the redteam gate as evidenced-but-not-truly-passed for revision 56.

openQuestions: Does the owner want to reactivate/rebuild the already-once-completed P1-011 dashboard work under a fresh Phase 2 spec, or start UI design from scratch? (REQ-dashboard-1 stays permanently reserved either way; only a new requirement ID could carry new dashboard behavior.)

Which exact 'Trigger model' does the owner want formalized for Phase 2 — true fixed-interval (every N minutes) vs. event-driven vs. a bounded standing authority the operator can pause? docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-31-phase-2-foundation-draft.md leaves this row explicitly open with no default toward automation.

Is 'Bybit' really a mis-transcription of 'buyback', or does the owner actually want a second, separate sale venue in addition to (or instead of) the Collector Crypt standard buyback? No repository evidence supports an actual Bybit integration.

Given ADR-0019's 'Operations never receives process principal', how does the owner intend a future fully-autonomous runner to hold signing authority for repeated cycles without becoming exactly the kind of un-owner-authorized standing custodian the current design forbids? This is the central architecture question Phase 2 must answer before any 20-minute loop can exist.

Should the stale (revision-55) red-team artifact set be regenerated against revision 56 before any further Phase 2 planning, given that RT-R55-02's severity assessment may have changed under the PegCycleVault redesign?

What should happen to a cycle that gets 'stuck' under real autonomous operation, given the current design's explicit position that a FAILED vault cycle has no recovery/withdrawal path and requires 'a separately specified immutable provider mechanism and fresh owner approval' to add one?
